sentences: Submissions that don't are closed without review.Minimal Contributor RequirementsEstablished account: your GitHub commit history is at least 6 months old.Proof of personhood: set an on-chain identity on the Polkadot People Chain for your AssetHub address and request a registrar judgement (official guide).
dotID does this for free, with social/email verification and optional KYC for a stronger judgement.

Autonomous agents that open PRs without a human reviewing and understanding the change are not eligible, regardless of disclosure.Be ready to explain your work: answer maintainers' review questions specifically and on topic within 5 days.

We will not review PRs that don't meet our quality standards.Fork the repository and create a new branch.Commit using a Conventional Commits message with a type and scope (see below), including the Signed-off-by and AI-Assisted-By trailers.In the PR description, explain in your own words the root cause of the bug and why your change fixes it.
A plain summary of the diff is not enough.Open a pull request referencing the issue and tag @michaeldev5 to request a review.Commit messages ​Write commit messages as type(scope): description.

Be sure to reserve it as outlined above before working on the fix.Can I use AI tools to help with my fix?Yes, using tools like GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude to help you write a fix is fine, as long as you disclose it via the AI-Assisted-By commit trailer, understand the code you're submitting, and can explain and defend it during review.

Submissions from autonomous agents that open PRs without a human reviewing and understanding the change first are not eligible, and repeated attempts will result in a permanent ban.What happens if I reserve an issue but don’t submit a PR in 48 hours?The issue becomes unreserved and open for others to claim.
The payment should be processed within 2 business days after the issue is resolved or the PR is merged.Need help?

We reward contributors for reporting and fixing bugs in the project.Report bugs$5–30Earn rewards based on bug severity.Fix bugs$5–250+Earn additional rewards based on fix complexity.Eligible tools ​These tools and apps from the xcm-tools monorepo are part of the Bug Bounty Program:XCM SDK (PAPI Version)SWAP ExtensionXCM APIXCM AnalyserXCM PlaygroundRequirements ​To keep the program focused on genuine human contributors, every bug report and fix must meet all of these requirements. Submissions that don't are closed without review.Minimal Contributor RequirementsEstablished account: your GitHub commit history is at least 6 months old.Proof of personhood: set an on-chain identity on the Polkadot People Chain for your AssetHub address and request a registrar judgement (official guide). dotID does this for free, with social/email verification and optional KYC for a stronger judgement. Maintainers check on Subscan that the judgement is at least Reasonable. Use the same address for payment; nothing outside the Polkadot ecosystem is needed.Signed commits: sign every commit in your PR with the -S flag and include this trailer:AI-Assisted-By: <tool name(s), e.g. "GitHub Copilot", "ChatGPT"> (or "None" if you didn't use one)AI tools are welcome, autonomous agents are not: using AI tools (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) is fine if you disclose it, understand the resulting code, and can explain and defend it yourself. Autonomous agents that open PRs without a human reviewing and understanding the change are not eligible, regardless of disclosure.Be ready to explain your work: answer maintainers' review questions specifically and on topic within 5 days. Without an answer, the reservation expires and the issue reopens for others. Generic, evasive, or off-topic answers get the PR closed and the reservation forfeited.Extra verification for high-severity fixes: for 🔴 High complexity fixes, maintainers may ask for a brief live chat or call walkthrough before payout, to confirm that a human authored the change and understands it.DANGERRepeated low-effort, undisclosed-AI, or automated submissions will result in a permanent ban from the Bug Bounty Program.Report a bug ​Open an issue in the repository and select Bug bounty report.Fill in all required sections.Submit the issue. Maintainers review it and assign a severity level.Rewards for reports ​Maintainers determine severity based on impact and may contact you for clarification.Very low$5–10Very minor errors in docs / text / codeLow$10–15Minor UI issues, typos, or cosmetic bugsMedium$15–20Bugs affecting user features or causing functional issuesHigh$20–30Crashes, data loss, security vulnerabilities, or major broken functionalityReporting or fixing grammar errors in the documentation that don't affect functionality or clarity isn't rewarded, but you're very welcome to open a PR fixing them.Fix a bug ​Reserving the IssueOnly issues with the "Bug bounty 💰" tag are eligible.Comment I would like to reserve this issue. on the issue. It is assigned to you and reserved for 48 hours; if no PR is opened by then, the reservation expires.You may reserve one issue at a time. Submit or drop your current reservation before reserving another; issues reserved in violation of this are reassigned.Reported the bug yourself? You still need to reserve the issue before fixing it.Someone already reported it or opened a PR? Comment to express intent and, if allowed, follow the same reservation and PR process. Keep your contribution additive and clearly explained.Submitting the FixMake sure your PR follows these rules and has high-quality code. We will not review PRs that don't meet our quality standards.Fork the repository and create a new branch.Commit using a Conventional Commits message with a type and scope (see below), including the Signed-off-by and AI-Assisted-By trailers.In the PR description, explain in your own words the root cause of the bug and why your change fixes it. A plain summary of the diff is not enough.Open a pull request referencing the issue and tag @michaeldev5 to request a review.Commit messages ​Write commit messages as type(scope): description. This helps automate changelog generation and keeps the project consistent.type is one of feat, fix, perf, revert, docs, style, chore, refactor, test, build or ci.scope is the package or app you changed, named after its folder in packages/ or apps/, for example sdk-core, sdk, assets, swap, xcm-api, xcm-analyser or playground.description says briefly what the commit does.For example, a signed fix in the SDK core package, with the Signed-off-by (-s) and AI-Assisted-By trailers:bashgit commit -S -s -m "fix(sdk-core): Handle null case in token parser" \ --trailer "AI-Assisted-By: None"What each commit type meansfeat: new features (Features)fix: bug fixes (Bug Fixes)perf: code changes that improve performance (Performance Improvements)revert: revert a previous commit (Reverts)docs: changes to documentation only (Documentation)style: code style changes such as formatting or whitespace (Styles)chore: routine tasks, hidden in changelogs (Miscellaneous Chores)refactor: code changes that neither fix bugs nor add features (Code Refactoring)test: adding or updating tests (Tests)build: changes that affect the build system or external dependencies (Build System)ci: CI configuration and scripts (Continuous Integration)Rewards for fixes ​Rewards depend on code complexity and quality, as determined by maintainers. The $250 for High complexity is not a hard cap: the final amount depends on the task and can be higher.Very low$5Very minor errors in docs / text / codeLow$10–20Small fix (e.g., 1-2 lines), config changesMedium$30–70Logic changes, multi-file fixes, test additionsHigh$80–250+Complex refactors, deep bug fixes, architectural or security-critical changes with tests and docsTips ​Follow the existing code style and structure.Write meaningful commit messages.Include unit tests if applicable.Keep PRs focused: one issue per pull request.Add inline comments on important changes and new functions.Be respectful and collaborative in discussions.FAQ ​Can I report and fix the same bug?Yes! You can both report and fix the bug. Be sure to reserve it as outlined above before working on the fix.Can I use AI tools to help with my fix?Yes, using tools like GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude to help you write a fix is fine, as long as you disclose it via the AI-Assisted-By commit trailer, understand the code you're submitting, and can explain and defend it during review. Submissions from autonomous agents that open PRs without a human reviewing and understanding the change first are not eligible, and repeated attempts will result in a permanent ban.What happens if I reserve an issue but don’t submit a PR in 48 hours?The issue becomes unreserved and open for others to claim. You may re-reserve it if it's still unassigned.How do you determine reward amounts?Bug reports are evaluated based on user impact and severity.Fixes are evaluated based on code complexity, design quality, and completeness (tests, documentation).How do I receive payment?Your payment will be sent to the AssetHub Polkadot address you provided in the issue or PR, and the amount will be paid in USDC. Please ensure you only provide non-cex addresses in the PR, because the payment may not arrive correctly. The payment should be processed within 2 business days after the issue is resolved or the PR is merged.Need help? ​If you're unsure how to start or have questions about an issue or PR, reach out through the contact form on our landing page, on our X, or in our Telegram support channel.We appreciate your support and contributions!The ParaSpell✨ Team Suggest changes to this pageLast updated:
